name: impact-based landing slice (prototype, not installed)
status: dry-run only: nothing runs this policy on a landing yet

checks: protected-paths (the controller's rsi/scenarios/protected, read at the base)
no-build-time-code (build.rs, .cargo/, a Cargo.toml build key, a new proc-macro)
test-count (the base's cargo test list cached by the base Rust tree)
core.cost: in setup; the test listing is a serial job only when the Rust tree changed and no base list is cached

path_classes.why: data the landing judge never reads: the backlog and nightly scenarios. A change needs the owner's review but cannot alter a landing verdict.
web tests and build read it
the build, the test listing and cargo tests read it
it shapes the judge, the toolchain or every job's environment: never accept a selection over it

historical.why: cache-only is today's gate plus content-addressed results: a historical scenario runs unless its inputs are unchanged and the base's accepting gate recorded a pass. nightly is the design-gate-v2 Decision 1 retirement; installing it needs the C9 proofs and the owner's switch.

nightly_holds.why: the proposed policy keeps real-time guardrail holds off the ordinary landing path (task 490 point 5; design-gate-v2 Decision 1). Until that install they are either cache hits (their inputs did not change) or run on the live path.

task_scenario.why: the task's own scenario must fail on the base and pass on the candidate (design-gate-v2 section 2). The live gate's 3-of-3 is P25, not part of this policy; --task-runs can model it.

non_goal: This file is not a live gate policy. gate.sh does not read it.
No check is retired by this file: historical scenarios are cache-only unless the operator selects the approved nightly mode.
Model text is never authority: selection comes only from git paths and content hashes.
